hero.title: GLA University
hero.summary: GLA’s agriculture faculty in Mathura connects crop science with field experiments, laboratory work and experiential study. Its undergraduate page highlights work with vegetables, herbs and flowers. A four-year degree, GLAET-based admission route and published 2026–27 academic fees give applicants concrete academic and cost details to compare.

overview.heading: Agriculture study and field learning at Mathura
paragraphs: GLA’s faculty page presents agriculture teaching around crop science, research and extension. It identifies field experiments, internships and industry exposure within its approach to experiential learning. The faculty also describes emerging areas such as precision agriculture and value addition, giving applicants a clearer picture than a general university overview alone.

The undergraduate page gives practical examples including vegetables, herbs and flowers, making the faculty’s crop-based work more tangible. Its entry criteria can be read alongside the 2026–27 Mathura fee schedule, which sets out academic charges for each of the four years. The faculty also describes postgraduate and doctoral teaching, allowing applicants to distinguish a broad first degree from later specialist study.

programmes.name: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture
programmes.summary: An agriculture degree with published field and laboratory learning elements.
programmes.eligibility: The official 2026 landing page states 10+2 with 50% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics/Agriculture, or a two-year agriculture diploma with 50%.

fees.includes: First-year academic fee for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture, Mathura campus.
fees.note: Published later-year academic fees are ₹85,000, ₹87,000 and ₹89,000. Examination, alumni, refundable caution and accommodation charges are separate; obtain the complete payable statement.
